tool.name: PyEuk distance
tool.description: compute a pairwise genetic-distance matrix from a haplotype sheet, PyEuk eukaryotyping
tool.command: pyeuk eukaryotyping --input-sheet '$sheet' --metric $metric --epsilon $epsilon --min-completeness $min_completeness --weight-mode $weight_mode --min-maf $min_maf #if str($ploidy).strip() != '' --ploidy $ploidy #end if #if $fasta --fasta '$fasta' #end if #if not $project_psd --no-psd #end if --output-matrix '$matrix'

param.name: sheet
param.label: Haplotype sheet
param.help: Specimen x haplotype presence/absence sheet, e.g. from the Build haplotype sheet tool.

param.name: weight_mode
param.label: Allele weighting
param.help: How informative each haplotype column is weighted. heterozygosity 2p(1-p) is correct for presence/absence input; the KING form is for centred dosages and should not be used here.

param.name: ploidy
param.label: Organism base ploidy
param.help: 1 for haploid (Cryptosporidium, bacteria), 2 for diploid. Leave blank for the engine default.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Reference / learned FASTA (snp-wibs only)
param.help: Required only for the snp-wibs metric; ignored otherwise.

param.name: min_completeness
param.label: Minimum locus completeness
param.help: A specimen must have this fraction of loci called to enter the matrix.

param.name: min_maf
param.label: Minimum minor-allele frequency
param.help: Filters near-invariant singleton columns. 0 = off (recommended under heterozygosity weighting).

param.name: project_psd
param.label: Project onto the PSD cone
param.help: OFF by default. Gram double-centering makes the distances embed in Euclidean space but compresses the closest pairs. Leave off for count-mode clustering; turn on with a distance cut.

tool.help:
**Turn a haplotype sheet into a pairwise distance matrix**
Compares only the windows called in both specimens and weights each haplotype by how much it varies within the cohort. The output is a square distance matrix you can feed to the **PyEuk cluster** tool.
The combined **PyEuk cluster** tool computes this matrix internally, so run this standalone tool only when you want the distance matrix on its own, or a metric or ploidy the combined tool does not expose (e.g. ``snp-wibs``, or an explicit ``--ploidy``). @HELP_FOOTER@
